title: In this town, you can buy anyone
format: narrative what-if (Larptuber 'In this town' one-rule world; fiction lane test #2)

hook.narration: In this town, everyone wears a price tag. Whoever pays it, owns you.

visual.v1: dusk town square wide (reuse #0010 night-town world DNA); every NPC carries a floating amber price tag (MAYOR $9,000,000 / SHERIFF $4,000 / folk $500-$2,000); hero dead-center, warm-lit, tag $1 gray; frame-0 title 'IN THIS TOWN,' / 'YOU CAN BUY ANYONE'; warm windows, long shadows; single-title hook law (L-128: title stamps own the frame at t=0, no other text competes)

scenes.narration: The Mayor cost nine million. The sheriff, four. I cost one dollar.

visual.v1: rapid triptych: mayor's mansion w/ glowing $9,000,000 tag -> sheriff w/ $4,000 -> hero alone, tiny $1; stamp '$1' (big gray)

scenes.narration: People used me as a tip jar.

visual.v1: two NPCs flick coins at the hero; one coin BOUNCES off the $1 tag (ping); NPCs smirk; hero face 100% neutral (deadpan law)

scenes.narration: Then a gray-coat stranger arrived, and started buying everyone.

visual.v1: the stranger enters frame-left: long gray coat, gray hat, ledger book; the ONLY fully desaturated object in town (color monopoly — the walking absence of value); first tag flips SOLD behind him

scenes.narration: The butcher. The sheriff. The choir. Sold. Sold. Sold.

visual.v1: three rapid shots: butcher tag, sheriff tag, choir row — SOLD stamp SLAMS on each (shake frames, dust puffs); gray-eyed townsfolk start lining up

scenes.narration: He skipped me. 'Not you. You're not for sale, you're the deposit.'

visual.v1: FAKE TWIST 1: stranger leans to hero eye level, ledger closed; quote stamp 'YOU'RE THE DEPOSIT'; hero's $1 tag pulses once; no answer given (tension deepens, never resolves)

scenes.narration: By midnight, the whole town marched behind him, gray-eyed.

visual.v1: wide night shot: gray procession down the main street, rows of SOLD tags bobbing; hero the only warm-lit figure, standing still; sky deepens

scenes.narration: At dawn, he handed me one dollar. Exact change.

visual.v1: THE TURN: pale-blue dawn palette (distinct from #0010 red-purge night); the stranger holds out a single bill between two fingers; stamp '$1 — EXACT CHANGE'

scenes.narration: I held it. The empty town held its breath.

visual.v1: HOLD (tension peak, zero resolution): extreme close on the bill in the hero's hand; around them the square is EMPTY, every window dark; 1.5s of near-silence (bed ducks)

scenes.narration: 'Full refund,' he said. 'The buyer backed out.'

visual.v1: FAKE TWIST 2: stranger tips his hat; quote stamp 'THE BUYER BACKED OUT'; behind him the gray townsfolk stand perfectly still, watching

scenes.narration: Then every tag in town flipped to the same number. One dollar.

visual.v1: THE MASS FLIP (money shot): a wave crosses the square back-to-front, every SOLD tag flipping to $1 in sequence (rapid tick cascade, 12-15 flips visible); hero watches, lit by the flip-wave

scenes.narration: The tags were never prices. They were installments.

visual.v1: REAL TWIST: hero looks UP at his own tag; it flips $1 -> 'PAID IN FULL' with a red-seal stamp slam (red reserved for THIS moment only — color monopoly); glass-shatter flash

scenes.narration: Everyone in this town has a price. I'm the price.

visual.v1: RULE RE-READ: hero walks alone through the parted gray crowd toward the town hall door (now his); quote stamp 'I'M THE PRICE'

scenes.narration: Tonight, I was finally paid off.

visual.v1: LOOP: tags dim out one row at a time behind him as he reaches the door; hard cut to BLACK on the last word — loop-to-black, no CTA, no end card
